newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela CVG confident of privatization this year.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela CVG confident of privatization this year.

text.p: Elias Ynaty, president of Venezuelan state-owned industrial giant Corporacion Venezolana de Guayana (CVG) said he was confident the company's slated $3 billion steel and aluminum privatizations would go ahead this year.
"I'm sure we'll get Congress' approval for their sale this year," Ynaty told the foreign press association.

The sales are widely seen as a test of the Venezuela's resolve to downsize its bloated public sector and follow through with structural reforms on the success of its macroeconomic stabilization program.

CVG steel company Sidor's sale contract is currently under discussion in Congress, Ynaty said. Contracts for the CVG's four aluminum companies -- Alcasa, Venalum, Carbonorca and Bauxilum -- should be submitted within a couple of weeks.
Base prices will be set shortly after the sales contracts' approval, and the sales themselves should go ahead two months after that, he added.
"There's a firm will for the sales to go ahead this year," Ynaty said.
Thirteen companies have qualified to bid for the aluminum companies, including Alcoa, Gencor Ltd, Alumax, Reynolds Metals Co, Norsk Hydro A/S and RTZ Corp.

Eleven companies have qualified for Sidor's sale, among them Mexico's Hylsamex SA, Imexsa, and Altos Hornos de Mexico SA ; Brazil's Usiminas, and Companhia Siderurgica Nacional ; Japan's Kobe Steel; Argentina's Rand Siderar SAIC ; and Venezuela's Sivensa.
